description:
FILED s430 (Fable, B3.3 review probe; PRE-EXISTING on 0b56ff9).

Reproducer (perl 5.40.3 prints PKG|, PCL prints |):

    { package Q; print main::nm(), "|\n"; } sub nm {"PKG"}

Without the `package Q;` (`{ print main::nm(), "|\n"; } sub nm {"PKG"}`) PCL is right, and so is a call from the same package.  Emission: the block with the package switch is emitted as its own section (`;;; package Q` / `(in-package :Q)`) and the hoisted `(p-sub pl-nm ...)` lands in the main section AFTER it, so at the call site only the forward `(p-declare-sub main::pl-nm)` stub exists -- which returns nothing instead of the sub, and nothing says so (no undefined-function error: the stub answers).  Two questions: (1) why the hoist order puts a file-level named sub after a block that precedes it in source (perl compiles every named sub before run time, so the order never matters there); (2) rule 12: a p-declare-sub stub called before its definition should DIE naming the sub, not answer undef -- that is what made this silent.  Found while writing lexical-sub-02.t row 5 (`package Q; print main::nm()` where a `my sub nm` is ALSO in scope -- the lexical is irrelevant, the minimal reproducer above has none).  Bar: the reproducer + the no-package-switch inverse vs perl; corpus-diff; the sweep if the hoist order changes (emission-wide).
=== s432 (Opus): HALF (a) SHIPPED.  HALF (b) still open â this task stays PENDING for it.

(a) THE STUB DIES, and first tries AUTOLOAD.  cl/pcl-runtime.lisp:
`%p-call-of-undefined-sub` + the p-declare-sub body.  perl's own order for a
plain sub call with no body: run the package's AUTOLOAD (with $AUTOLOAD set to
the qualified name and the original @_ â and NO @ISA walk, that is the method
rule), and only when the package has no AUTOLOAD is it fatal.  So:

    { package Q; print main::nm(), "|\n"; } sub nm {"PKG"}
        before: prints "|"      after: dies "Undefined subroutine &main::nm called."
    sub nope; nope();
        before: undef, rc 0     after: perl's own message (perl dies too)
    sub foo; sub AUTOLOAD {...} foo()
        before: undef           after: AUTO(main::foo)   <- perl's answer

`\&foo` is unaffected: p-backslash-sub hands back a TRAMPOLINE that re-reads
symbol-function at call time, so a coderef taken on a stub still reaches a body
defined later.  p-can / p-stash / p-coderef-defined-p already skip :stub.

MEASURED: gate 160 files / 5703 rows (the 3 new guard rows in
Pl/t/decl-ordering-02.t; only the 13 pclxs xs rows fail).  Full sweep: ONE row
moved anywhere -- sort.t 203 -> 202, an ACCIDENTAL pass (bug 36430's
`sort { A::min(@$a) <=> A::min(@$b) }` runs before the `package A; sub min` in
its own block, both calls hit the stub, undef <=> undef = 0, the list came back
unsorted and the assertion only checked that a flag stayed "good").  Edited into
docs/pass-baseline.tsv by hand with that cause.  In the other direction the fix
let perl-tests/sort.t's `ok(1, "SKIP: stubborn AUTOLOAD ...")` be RESTORED to
perl's own assertion (`sort stubbedsub split//, '04381091'` -> '98431100'),
which passes now.

(b) THE HOIST ORDER â MEASURED, NOT FIXED.  The mechanism is Pl/Parser2.pm's
"Cross-section forward sub calls" block (the one that emits
`(pcl:p-declare-sub Pkg::pl-name)` in the file prologue).  Its comment already
names the case: an earlier section's load-time code may call a sub a LATER
section defines.  It hoists the DECLARATION so the form is readable; the
DEFINITION stays in its own section, which is why the call runs against a stub.

POPULATION (measured s432 over 722 files: perl-tests + perl's t/ default dirs +
lib/ + cpan-tests/modules): **75 files emit at least one such stub**, most of
them tie/DESTROY/AUTOLOAD callbacks where the call happens after the whole file
has loaded (so the stub is never entered).  Only sort.t's bug-36430 row entered
one in the whole sweep.

FIX SHAPE for (b): in that same block, emit the sub's DEFINITION in the prologue
instead of (or besides) the stub, wrapped in its own `(in-package :X)` ...
`(in-package :pcl)` pair -- in-package is read-time per top-level form, so this
is exactly what the section assembly already does, and it is the only way to
keep the body's free symbols resolving in their own package.  Redefinition is
idempotent (p-sub setfs symbol-function), so the def may stay in its section
too.  Risk to probe first: a body that references a defvar its section declares
later (readable, but SBCL will warn), and compile time (the def is compiled
twice).  BAR: the reproducer + the no-package-switch inverse vs perl;
corpus-diff; the emission moves for those 75 files -> full sweep + the
four-population A/B with every diff explained per file.  When it lands, sort.t's
bug-36430 row comes back as an HONEST pass and the two #456 guard rows in
Pl/t/decl-ordering-02.t become one both_agree row (the guard says so).


=== s433 (Fable) RULING on half (b): PROMOTED to session Q3 (plan-post-s433), before P3.  SHAPE RULED = perl's PHASE model across sections (#469 is the general form, filed from the BEGIN probe; closes with this task): every section's compile-phase forms (decls, captured, defs, sched) before any section's run-phase forms, each group under its own (in-package) switches, MOVE never copy.  The s432 "emit the DEF in the prologue" sketch is UNSAFE: a body above its section's decls compiles a p-defcell SYMBOL-MACRO as a free variable (probed).  Fallback = on-demand hoist of the needed section's decls+defs, never the def alone.  Ask 1 (AUTOLOAD before die) CONFIRMED; Ask 2 (guard shape) RIGHT as shipped; Ask 3 (rule 12 at -94 rows) CONFIRMED, the 94 are #467's.  Full text: docs/fable-answers-s433.md Â§B.


=== half (b) DONE s436 (Opus 5), commit b95ad91, together with #469 (the
general form).  Pl::Parser2::parse's section assembly runs in TWO PASSES: every
section's COMPILE phase, then (p-run-compile-phase-blocks), then every
section's RUN phase.  `{ package Q; print main::nm(), "|\n"; } sub nm {"PKG"}`
prints PKG| like perl.  See #469 for the full record.
subject: A qualified call `main::nm()` inside a block-scoped `package Q;` region, to a sub DEFINED LATER at file level, returns EMPTY (silent wrong; perl PKG)
